examples: Months later the project comes back: unpack folder checks the archive's checksum, restores every file, and moves the archive to the Trash.
how_to: Hide (archive) the project first; only hidden projects can be packed.
Open the project's menu on the projects page and choose pack folder. The plan checks for live sessions, unpushed or modified git work, cloud-only files and free space, and shows what will happen.

A repo with no remote asks a second question: the archive will be the only copy. Confirm to pack; the originals go to the Trash only after every file in the archive is checked against a sha256 manifest.
A packed project shows a packed tag with the archive size. If the archive is changed or missing outside Carnivore the tag turns into a warning, and the unpack confirmation repeats it.
Choose unpack folder to restore. The archive checksum is compared first; a modified archive is refused and nothing is extracted.
media_exempt: its screen is the projects page's project menu and the shared confirm dialog; no recapture is run for it until the pre-release pipeline
name: Pack a project's folder
summary: compress a hidden project's folder in place into one archive to free disk space, with git, live-session and cloud-only refusals, a per-file checksum check before the originals go to the Trash, and a warning when the archive was changed outside carnivore.
where: Projects page: a hidden project's menu, pack folder / unpack folder; POST /api/v1/projects/{name}/pack and /unpack.
